newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- DEC 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- DEC 12.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--The latest quarterly report by the Foundation of Industrial and Economic Research (IOBE) tells the government that its mix of economic policies has reached its limits in fighting inflation and that the new budget does not do enough in cutting back on spending.
--Ruling party PASOK and government have turned all their attention to "facilitating" protesting farmers in an effort to get them off the road blocks and back on the farm, sources say.

--Two major Korean firms, including the Daewoo Group, have expressed firm interest in the sale of the Bank of Crete. Reports say that the two have bombarded the bank and ministry with questions about the forthcoming sale.
--The Mortgage Bank is working on repayment adjustments for 10,000 home loan customers, offering favourable terms for prompt repayment and write-offs.
IMERISIA

--The continuing farmers' blockade - now in its 15th day - has caused irreparable harm to the economy and appears to be about to undermine the economic policies and budget for next year. A joint press conference today will appeal to the farmers to end their blockade and to the government to change tack and find a solution.
--A new survey says that the wholesale abolition of tax breaks would have brought over two trillion drachmas annually to state coffers.

--The last bond auction for the year and the final offer of non-taxable state titles will take place at the end of the month. The finance ministry will offer seven-year bonds and is considering auctioning three-year fixed-rate bonds. The first issue of the new year is slated for January 2.
--Greece's own One Stop Shop has begun business with investments of 160 billion: the Greek Investment Centre says it will open the way to foreign investors.
KERDOS

--The significant increase in lending by businesses - particularly in foreign exchange - is another factor that works against bringing inflation down, IOBE notes. Firms resorting to forex loans have been forced there by high domestic interest rates and the continuing 'hard drachma' policy.
--The conflict between farmers and government has taken on a political flavour with opposition party leaders visiting the blockades to offer support.
EXPRESS

--A wide-ranging meeting at the agriculture ministry on the cotton issue is the government's latest overture to the farmers. However, reports say that farmers do not want to become involved in 'unofficial' talks.
--The new bill on taxation measures may be amended further following the finance ministry's memo to directorates to submit their additional comments on possible oversights and loopholes.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--Exporters in northern Greece speak of up to 150 billion drachmas in losses from the farmers' blockade and request the intervention of the courts.

--The truth of the state of the economy must be explained to the Greek people to garner their support for economic policies, Athens Chamber president says. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
